entities.summary: Gaius Calpurnius Piso was a Roman senator and a key figure in the Pisonian conspiracy of AD 65, a plot that shook the Roman Empire to its core. The plot, which involved a complex web of alliances and rivalries between Roman senators, aimed to overthrow Emperor Nero and restore the traditional Roman Republic. Piso, who was a member of the senatorial class and a close friend of Emperor Claudius, played a crucial role in the plot, using his connections and influence to gather support among other senators. However, the plot ultimately failed, and Piso was arrested and executed in AD 65. The Pisonian conspiracy had a lasting impact on Roman history, leading to a period of increased instability and power struggles in the Roman Empire. The event also led to the downfall of Emperor Claudius, who was forced to take his own life to avoid being implicated in the plot. The Pisonian conspiracy remains one of the most infamous and studied examples of political intrigue in Roman history.
